title: Subjuntivo tras expresiones de necesidad y valoración

sections.content: Expressions like era necesario que, era importante que, no era extraño que and convenía que all evaluate a fact rather than simply report it — and any time the main clause evaluates instead of asserting, the verb that follows que goes into the subjunctive. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Era necesario que la población reconociera esos símbolos como propios.
items.english: It was necessary for the population to recognize those symbols as their own.

items.spanish: Era esencial, para el nuevo Estado mexicano, que ese pasado prehispánico se convirtiera en fuente de orgullo nacional.
items.english: It was essential, for the new Mexican state, for that pre-Hispanic past to become a source of national pride.

items.spanish: No era extraño que el pasado indígena fuera glorificado al mismo tiempo que el presente indígena era ignorado.
items.english: It wasn't strange that the indigenous past was glorified at the same time the indigenous present was ignored.

items.spanish: Convenía a las élites que el pasado prehispánico se percibiera como una civilización gloriosa pero clausurada.
items.english: It suited the elites for the pre-Hispanic past to be perceived as a glorious but closed-off civilization.

sections.content: Compare era necesario que reconociera (subjunctive, because the main clause judges the fact) with the plain statement la población reconoció esos símbolos (indicative, just reporting what happened). The judgment word in the main clause — necesario, esencial, extraño, convenía — is what triggers the subjunctive that follows.
